Current metrics development fixtures

These fixtures are opt-in development tools. The application never installs Metrics Server or requires these scripts.

Inspect kubectl --context kind-dev-local-a get --raw /apis/metrics.k8s.io first. Reuse an existing provider. If absent, run scripts/metrics-fixtures.sh setup kind-dev-local-a. The script rejects every pre-existing resource before creating anything, and refuses other contexts. A failed partial setup retains its UID inventory for cleanup. Do not delete that inventory before cleanup.

The pinned upstream Metrics Server 0.8.1 manifest SHA-256 is 4a672c4891902573a3ff753cece5de1bf1f55dd053403dfec39df9d1636b7ff1; the multi-platform image digest is sha256:b2d2efaf5ac3b366ed0f839d2412a2c4279d4fc2a2a733f12c52133faed36c41. Upstream supports Kubernetes 1.31 and later. The added --kubelet-insecure-tls flag is only for disposable kind kubelet certificates; application transport trust is unchanged.

Only after confirming the namespace is absent, create synthetic workloads and restricted core-reader RBAC with an explicit approved context. Use the same namespace/name on A and B. Never apply over an existing fixture. Record namespace UID, then export each approved context into a private isolated a.kubeconfig or b.kubeconfig. A token for the fixture service account in a-denied.kubeconfig proves metrics denial alongside a permitted Pod read. Tokens and configs belong only in ignored run evidence. Wait for the provider and Pod readiness before the opt-in check.

Run scripts/metrics-fixtures.sh --self-test, then KUBESIFT_METRICS_INTEGRATION=1 KUBESIFT_EXPLORER_CONFIG_DIR=/absolute/private/run go test -tags=integration ./tests/integration -run '^TestCurrentMetrics$' -count=1 -v. This walkthrough expects A to provide metrics and B to demonstrate absence; if B already has a provider, preserve it and adapt the absence check to deterministic coverage instead.

Provider cleanup: scripts/metrics-fixtures.sh cleanup kind-dev-local-a. Each deletion uses its recorded UID precondition; replacements and unrelated resources are preserved. Remove only owned workload namespace UIDs separately with Kubernetes DeleteOptions preconditions. The script's ignored inventory survives interruption. Registry/image-loading problems and any explicit local image substitution must be recorded in the phase report, including the upstream binary checksum and actual image identity.
